clue.text: Cook's been able to do this once on time (common gender question posed by society!)

definitions.text: Cook's been able to do this once

parts.note: RE means on or concerning
spelt informally, 'Ain't he a she?' is a question about someone's gender, in common speech

explanation.surface: A cookery note seems to break off into a joke about social attitudes to gender.
explanation.walkthrough: Alastair Cook captained England, who kept the Ashes, cricket's England-Australia trophy, in 2013. 'common' means colloquial: AIN'T HE A SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: England under captain Alastair Cook kept cricket's Ashes urn, so that is what Cook once managed to do.

clue.text: Freshly hassled, gets even: divorces bride — so saying?

indicators.note: freshly suggests the words are made over anew, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone, harassed again, takes revenge by divorcing the bride, and the clue asks whether a proverb covers it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freshly' rearranges all twenty-eight letters of 'hassled gets even divorces bride'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says vengeance is better taken later, calmly; it is a well-known adage.

clue.text: Old mortar in building programme co-tenant's brought up

indicators.note: brought up says the hidden letters are read backwards, upwards in a down light
in building says the answer sits within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Old mortar is found in a building scheme that a co-tenant raised.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Old mortar in building' as the definition; 'in building' is the hiding signal, so the definition is just 'Old mortar'.
explanation.definitionFit: First World War signallers' alphabet said T as Toc and M as Emma, so a trench mortar was a Toc Emma.

clue.text: Mannequins I de-legitimised, having the measure of men's outfitter

indicators.note: having means the words that come before it hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: Someone discredits shop dummies, armed with a tailor's measurements.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor measures the length from crotch to ankle when fitting trousers for a client.

clue.text: Moving about

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both emotionally affecting and, as a preposition, regarding a matter.

clue.text: Last divers under base

indicators.note: divers is the old word for various or different, so the letters of under are varied

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: Divers come last, under the base of operations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' is not people diving but the adjective meaning sundry.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to continue or persist through time, a verb synonym.

clue.text: With intervention of government, this goes up a great deal

indicators.note: intervention means one thing comes between others, so a letter is put inside
in a down light, going up means the word this is read backwards

explanation.surface: A political remark: once the state intervenes, the cost rises sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes up' turns THIS into SIHT, and 'With intervention of' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adverbially, as in 'a sight better', the word means by a lot or considerably.

clue.text: Articles praising one in United goal getting drunk after end of game

indicators.note: after puts the anagram behind the letter from game
end of picks the final letter of the word game

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

indicators.note: in puts the letter for one inside the other pieces
getting drunk means the letters become disordered, staggering into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Match reports praise a United player whose goal led to celebratory drinking after the final whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I into GOAL, and 'getting drunk' rearranges those five letters into LOGIA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a plural of eulogium, a speech or writing in praise of someone.

clue.text: See 1
Police who want use of crackdown say they are gripping the court!

definitions.text: Police who want use of crackdown

parts.note: vices are bench tools that grip work tightly
a quad is a quadrangle, a courtyard of a college

explanation.surface: Police wanting a crackdown are said to be holding on to the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks VICES as an example: vices are things that grip.
explanation.definitionFit: This police unit targets vice, so it wants to clamp down on the use of drugs and prostitution.

clue.text: Sri Lankan port's lifeboat's chief caught in a force 8

indicators.note: caught in means one piece is held inside another

parts.note: force 8 on the Beaufort scale of wind speed is a gale

indicators.note: chief means the head, the first letter of lifeboat

explanation.surface: A port's lifeboat leader gets caught out in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Galle is a fortified harbour town on the southern coast of Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Itinerant #out to lunch

parts.note: the hash symbol stands for number, abbreviated No.
out to lunch is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A wanderer is away at lunch, as if on a social-media hashtag.
explanation.definitionFit: A roaming person with no fixed home moves from place to place, as an itinerant does.

clue.text: Play this for eventual gain and drag to the ground

indicators.note: ground is the past tense of grind, so these letters are crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: Tactics in a tussle: let them pull you down for later advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like the noun after 'to the' but signals the anagram of DRAGTOTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Feigning a lack of interest to make oneself more desirable is the idiom 'play' this way in courtship.

clue.text: World traveller's not doing too well in business with PC?

parts.note: ET, the extraterrestrial of the film, is a traveller between worlds
ailing means unwell

explanation.surface: A globetrotter's firm is struggling in the computer trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Online retail is selling goods over the internet, trade done with a personal computer.

clue.text: High-class clothes business — right time to go for it!

indicators.note: to go means those letters leave the word

parts.note: the rag trade is a slang name for the fashion industry

explanation.surface: A smart fashion house decides the right moment has come to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' and 'time to go' remove R and T from RAG TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A top grade in an exam means first-rate, so the term describes excellent quality.

clue.text: Indulge too much in what's unusually legal of mafioso

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the rearranged letters
unusually means the letters appear in an uncommon order

parts.note: OD is short for overdose, to take too much

explanation.surface: A gangster overindulges in something oddly legal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' makes GOFELLA, split around OD: an overdose is taking too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster in Mafia slang, made famous by the Scorsese film, is a made member of the mob.

clue.text: "N", some out of uniform inspiring Sussex resort with no hotel

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so one piece takes another inside it
out of means the letter leaves the word

parts.note: a number of things means some of them
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: with no means the letter is dropped

parts.note: Hove is a seaside town next to Brighton in East Sussex
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Some people out of uniform get ideas at a south-coast town without a place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of uniform' leaves NMBER and 'with no hotel' leaves OVE; 'inspiring' (breathing in) puts OVE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet used by radio operators, the letter N is spoken as this month's name.

clue.text: Fitful earless driving programme through well

indicators.note: through means one piece passes inside another

parts.note: so, like well, starts a sentence

indicators.note: earless means without the letters ear

parts.note: Top Gear is the BBC motoring television show

explanation.surface: A motoring show plays deaf, stuttering on and off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earless' takes EAR from TOP GEAR, leaving TOPG.
explanation.definitionFit: Proceeding in starts and halts, the term describes irregular, interrupted progress.

clue.text: The Queen's personal circle has no news to broadcast

parts.note: O is a circle shape

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Royal insiders have nothing to tell the media.
explanation.walkthrough: The monarch traditionally says 'one' for herself, so her 'my own' becomes this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal 'one' replaces 'my', so 'personal' or 'private' in the monarch's mouth is this phrase.

clue.text: Look into enclosed space and see transmitter

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a court is a yard enclosed by walls
lo is an old word meaning look
v is short for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: An instruction: peer into a yard to spot a radio mast.
explanation.definitionFit: A television set relays broadcast pictures in full hues, here loosely called something that transmits images.

clue.text: Outstanding piece of fiction concerning upset on borders

indicators.note: on borders means the other piece lies along both edges of this one
upset in a down light means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: over means concerning, as in a row over money
a lie is an invented story

explanation.surface: A notable novel extract concerns a frontier upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' gives REVO, and 'on borders' has it flank the fiction on both sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief sculpture has figures projecting from a background, so the work stands out from its surface.

clue.text: Received refreshment at 4pm on 1/4, oh yesssss!

parts.note: got means received
cha is tea, the British afternoon refreshment

explanation.surface: Someone got afternoon tea on the first of April and is delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 1/4 is the British date 1 April, April Fools' Day, when pranksters shout their triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: This triumphant cry is what a prankster says after catching someone out on April Fools' Day.

clue.text: On vacation, double-crossed nasty DJ?

indicators.note: nasty means the letters are messed up into a new order
on vacation means emptied, so only the outer letters of double stay

explanation.surface: A betrayed disc jockey turns spiteful.
explanation.walkthrough: DJ is a dinner jacket. 'On vacation' empties DOUBLE to DE; 'nasty' rearranges DE and CROSSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Black tie, a dinner jacket, is an example of the rule for what guests must wear.

clue.text: Parents' progeny? Some of it

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Children are the parents' offspring, and here a few letters are enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'it' as the definition; 'it' refers back to 'Parents' progeny', which both defines and hides the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A child is a slang synonym for offspring in British usage.

clue.text: International ran laps on record

indicators.note: laps means wraps around, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: fled means ran away

explanation.surface: An athlete in an international meet ran laps for the records.
explanation.definitionFit: Documents put away in an archive are stored and kept as an official recorded copy.

clue.text: Timeless band's backing track

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word reads backwards
timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: troops are bands of soldiers

explanation.surface: A musical group's backing track never dates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' removes T from TROOPS; 'backing' reverses ROOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The trail of a wild animal, its prints or droppings, is what hunters follow.

clue.text: One intriguing old Spanish gentleman

parts.note: a caballer is one who plots as part of a cabal

explanation.surface: A scheming old Spanish nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a knight or horseman is used for a gentleman.

clue.text: Virginia back, cutting Myra, is getting involved with Gordon — TV feature?

indicators.note: cutting means pushing into the middle of another piece
getting involved means the letters are tangled into a new order
back means the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: VA is the US state code for Virginia

explanation.surface: A woman returning from Virginia interrupts Myra, who is having an affair with Gordon: soap-opera stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives AV, which 'cutting' puts inside the anagram SNOGMARRYOID.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a BBC Three makeover reality television programme, so it was a feature on the box.
